chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from Abī Maryam, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام ruled that in cases of lampooning, there is taʿzīr.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام as commander of the believers
key_terms.التَّعْزِيرَ: discretionary punishment imposed for an offense not carrying a fixed hadd penalty
key_terms.الْهِجَاءِ: lampooning, satirical or insulting speech directed at others

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on lampooning or insulting speech in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling from Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام concerning verbal abuse or lampooning. It establishes that such conduct is subject to taʿzīr, meaning a discretionary punishment determined by lawful authority.
